chunks: And from him, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, who said: 'Not one of the companions of Ali ibn Abi Hamzah narrated to me from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah that he asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the woman who is divorced in a non-Sunnah manner: 'Does the man marry her?' He said: 'Adhere to them in that which they adhered to themselves, and marry them, for there is no harm in that.'

Al-Hasan said: 'I heard Ja'far ibn Sam'ah asked about a woman who was divorced in a non-Sunnah manner: 'Is it for me to marry her?' He said: 'Yes.' I said to him: 'Do you not know that Ali ibn Hanzalah narrated: 'Beware of the thrice-divorced women who are divorced in a non-Sunnah manner, for they are women with husbands'?' He said: 'O my son, the narration of Ali ibn Abi Hamzah is more expansive for the people.' I said: 'And what did Ali ibn Abi Hamzah narrate?' He said: 'He narrated from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) that he said: 'Adhere to them in that which they adhered to themselves, and marry them, for there is no harm in that.'.'

key_terms.أَلْزِمُوهُمْ: Adhere to them / Make them stick to
key_terms.ذَوَاتُ أَزْوَاج: Women with husbands (implying they are not fully free but not permanently barred)
key_terms.عَلَى غَيْرِ السُّنَّة: In a non-Sunnah manner (referring to triple divorce in one sitting)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying a woman who received a triple divorce in a non-Sunnah manner?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the jurisprudential nuance between the strict narration of Ali ibn Hanzalah, which viewed non-Sunnah triple divorce as creating a barrier, and the more lenient, expansive ruling of Ali ibn Abi Hamzah transmitted from Imam al-Sadiq (AS). The Imam’s directive to 'bind them to what they bound themselves to' establishes that the husband retains the option to remarry directly without requiring a full intervening marriage (Nikah al-Mut'ah), reflecting a practical easing of the law for the community. This distinction underscores the Shia scholarly principle of reconciling apparent contradictions in hadith by prioritizing the more permissive interpretation when it aligns with the Imam's broader intent.
